Alex — thanks for the fast report and attachments. We’re looking now. Top-level notes from initial telemetry:
- We see a batch pattern shift at 08:27 PT where average batch sizes fell but per-token kernel time increased (possible kernel-selection path change).
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~35% for hot prefixes correlated with your peak traffic windows.
- p95 aligns to a subset of requests using long-context prompts (>=4k tokens).

Immediate actions we will try (and why):
1) Apply temporary routing to a smaller model variant with lower sequence-cost for the payment flow (mitigates p95 impact).
2) Enable conservative prefix/KV caching policy for hot prefixes to restore hit rate.
3) Increase concurrency pool by +10% for your dedicated nodes to cover transient backlog.

We’ll apply 1+2 in the next 15 minutes and monitor. CCing Marissa (CS lead) and Jonas (SRE/runtime) to take ownership on the rollout and to prepare an exec one-pager if we need leadership support.

Can you confirm whether you deployed any client-side prompt-changes at ~20:00 PT last night? That will help rule out prompt-side regressions.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick technical findings and recommended action:
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden kernel-selection inferences are hitting a slower kernel path for long-context decode (observed on ~12% of hot requests). Combined with increased KV cache churn (TTL mis-match after last config), this produced queueing and elevated tail latency.
- Evidence: per-shard kernel time graphs (attached to the JIRA ticket) show a step-change at 08:26 PT. KVcache eviction rate spiked at same time.

Recommended immediate plan (minutes):
1) Pin payment-route to small-model variant (already done).
2) Temporarily set KV cache TTL from 30s -> 300s for hot prefixes (we rolled a 60m policy earlier; propose a targeted 5m TTL to avoid memory blowout).
3) Apply kernel flag override on a single rack (non-disruptive flag flip) and observe; if good, expand rolling window. This requires a short controlled restart per pod.

I’ve created JIRA RB-4321 and uploaded kernel metrics + the suggested runbook: runbook_kvcache_rollout.pdf. If the customer is ok with a 10-minute restart window per rack we can attempt the kernel override now; otherwise we continue with routing + cache TTL.

— Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
